audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted their own why-text: level 1 read Jax while whys[0] calls it 'your weakest window'; levels 2, 3 and 4-5 read Skill/Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench while whys[1] through whys[3] describe Counter Strike coming online and out-duelling him; level 6 read Jax while whys[4] says 'it tightens here'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Jax/Jax/Jax/Skill/Tahm Kench/Tahm Kench at 50.82% over 795 games — your window is 2 through 5, his is from the first item onward as his sustain outgrows your DPS.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Skill / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench in both layers, ratings realigned to 5, 7, 7, 7, 5, 3, 3.

Consistent with the mirror's finding that your level 4-5 strength is Relentless Assault's attack-speed ramp rather than any ultimate, and that the ultimate's Armor/MR is an activation while the third-attack magic damage is the passive half — spikes[1] already frames it that way.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors. (1) early and wants.you[0] tell you to hold Counter Strike for 'his walk-up autos and his Tongue Lash' — Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only, so Tongue Lash lands through it and still applies its An Acquired Taste stack. (2) Abyssal Dive is called 'his escape + shield' — it is a knockup dive, an engage, and the shield is Thick Skin. (3) Devour is repeatedly written as 'W-Devour'; Devour is his R.
audit.why: Riot's texts: Counter Strike dodges all incoming attacks; Tongue Lash is a 900-range tongue on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s that damages, slows, heals him and applies a stack, stunning at three stacks. Abyssal Dive (21/20/19/18/17s) dives and knocks up. Thick Skin is a 3s-cooldown conversion of stored damage into a shield — it is effectively always available, which is why short pokes are worthless and only committed bursts pay. Devour is the ultimate, gated by three passive stacks and 100 mana rather than by a cooldown. The mirror audit independently flagged the same Counter Strike confusion as the worst line on its page.
audit.corrected: early, wants.you[0] and report[5].t now state that Counter Strike does not blank Tongue Lash; breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d re-describe Abyssal Dive as a knockup engage and add Thick Skin's 3s shield; whys[5] and spikes[3].text now call Devour by its correct slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tracked cooldown was described wrongly and carried no number.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive at 21s rank 1 is his longest cooldown and the one worth punishing; Thick Skin at 3s is never a window at all, which is the more useful thing for the reader to know.

edits.before: Auto-trade only with E held in your pocket. Identify how Tahm Kench contests the first waves before you commit anything.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Abyssal Dive's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Ranking E keeps the dodge-stun up more often, and your R's resists plus the third-hit magic proc beat his regen at the all-in.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tahm Kench's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: It tightens: your Trinity spike is real, but his first tank item and health-scaling passive match your damage — all-in only on his Q stun down.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Tahm Kench carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He out-scales into a peel-tank and Abyssal Dive lets him flank — unless you ended early he wins the map while losing the 1v1.

edits.before: Tahm Kench is a slow sustain tank, not a kiter, so Counter Strike does real work here — that changes the lane. At level 1 just farm and watch how he contests the wave. From level 2 hold your E for his walk-up autos and his Tongue Lash: dodge the hits he needs to build his 3-stack Q stun, recast for your own stun, then Q-in with an Empowered hit. At 3 your full combo owns the extended trade — but his grey-health passive and natural tank regen heal poke right back, so commit hard or you net nothing.
edits.after: Tahm Kench is a slow sustain tank, not a kiter, so Counter Strike does real work here — that changes the lane. At level 1 just farm and watch how he contests the wave. From level 2 hold your E for his walk-up autos; it will not blank Tongue Lash, so he still stacks you toward the stun — dodge the autos, recast for your own stun, then Q-in with an Empowered hit. At 3 your full combo owns the extended trade — but Thick Skin banks the damage you deal and hands it straight back as a shield, so commit hard or you net nothing.
